Q1: The ledger's malformed-marker check only reads a comment's first line, but the plan puts the new header second-to-last. How should the plan resolve this?
Choices:
- A: Keep the header and marker as the last two lines, as written. Add the header to `GUARD_REJECTION_HEADERS` as planned; it is inert there and documents the header. Change the ledger test so that the header without a marker never offers `override_guard`, with reason `missing` instead of `malformed`. No other ledger change. (RECOMMENDED)
- B: Keep the header and marker as the last two lines, and make one small extra change to `scripts/unblock_ledger.py`: also treat a comment as a rejection header when the line before the last is an entry in `GUARD_REJECTION_HEADERS`. This changes all three call sites (lines 600, 686, 746), so the malformed check covers planning comments as the issue intended. This goes against the issue's "make no other ledger change".
- C: When the block is routed, put the header first and the marker last. The ledger works unchanged, but the routed comment no longer starts with `Planning blocked: human input required.` The first-line match at `unblock_judge.sh:599` is only used for `stop=blocked`, and a routed item is `scope-blocked`. A new contract test would need to pin the routed layout.
